_: GutLog v3.18.0, server side. Four of the seven assertions are about
behaviour v3.17.0 did not have: it sent a tile for every metric whether
or not the metric held anything, and its footnote argued from a rhythm
claim that is not current. Against the reconstructed v3.17.0 each of the
Assertions 04 and 05 guard the OTHER direction -- that the new rule does
not throw away a tile that does hold something. v3.17.0 threw nothing
away, so no version control can make them fail; the withholding test is
widened from AND to OR in a copy of the current app instead, and both
catch it. That is the risk worth controlling here: a change that stops
drawing empty tiles is one line away from a change that stops drawing.
Assertion 06 is the one that would otherwise prove nothing. 'load_hours
appears once an operating day is logged' was true of v3.17.0 as well --
it appeared whether or not anything was logged -- so the assertion is on
the PAIR, absent before and present after, which only a build that
withholds the empty tile can satisfy.
Assertion 07 guards the login on /api/watch, which v3.17.0 already had,
so it is broken on purpose in a copy of the current app instead.

assertions.name: 01 the footnote gives the honest reason and claims nothing about rhythm
